summary: Verified core search, discovery, and pagination concepts: SQL injection risks of dynamic string concatenation vs parameter binding and identifier allowlisting, necessity of bounding page_size to prevent buffer pool exhaustion, and operational tradeoffs/dual-write consistency risks of dedicated search engines.
evidence: Explained SQL injection vulnerability with string concatenation and articulated how parameter binding protects query values while strict allowlists protect dynamic SQL identifiers (columns and sort order).
Justified bounded pagination (max page_size = 100, default = 20) to protect database memory, CPU, and buffer pool from unbounded query exhaustion and Denial-of-Service.

Analyzed the operational costs and synchronization risks of dedicated search engines (dual writes, replication lag, eventual consistency) versus immediate DB-native consistency for URL shortener requirements.
